admitted.text: Vee reads as newly voracious for pleasure, food, beauty, and attention after years of mistaking deprivation for virtue.
admitted.detail_quote: She had spent the entire afternoon being seen at her most ashamed and had not, once, been found wanting.

admitted.text: Vee's mother seems to be the source of the shaming voice Vee carries inside her.
admitted.detail_quote: the word arriving whole and in her mother's voice before she had finished forming the picture

admitted.text: Vee reads as a quick, practiced explainer-away of Randi's kisses, which suggests there is something she needs to explain away.
admitted.detail_quote: It's a French thing, she does the kiss-kiss, she's been everywhere, that's all it is, that's just how women like her say goodbye.

admitted.text: The kiss in the foyer reads as Vee's body getting ahead of every explanation she has built.
admitted.detail_quote: under all those framed faces Vee kissed her best friend until the thing in her chest had somewhere to go.

admitted.text: Vee reads as tender and discreet; she shields Randi from shame she did nothing to earn.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't look back at the point, and she didn't say the name

admitted.text: Her account of the reconciliation reads as smoothed over: a happy surface laid over the unsaid word.
admitted.detail_quote: The same name he'd said behind her in December as she walked out his door — the one that hadn't been the word she'd come for then, and hadn't been enough.

admitted.text: Pace reads as loving Vee already, with his refusal to say so rooted in old loss rather than lack of feeling.
admitted.detail_quote: He had hurt her because he was afraid of how much she could hurt him.

admitted.text: Pace seems sincere about consent, repeatedly leaving choices open even when his desire is strong.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: Pace reads as a man who sees Vee clearly and with real tenderness.
admitted.detail_quote: she's the most alive person standing there, and it never once occurs to her.

admitted.text: reads as a reader of women — he watched Randi's face when he pointed at Vee, and the reader is invited to wonder how much of his tenderness is aimed observation
admitted.detail_quote: You clever bastard — you had me picking women off a lawn in broad daylight, and I was delighted with myself the whole way.

admitted.text: With Randi's distress he seems to settle for the easy explanation, which reads as a convenient blindness.
admitted.detail_quote: He let it be hormones.

admitted.text: His withdrawal in loud places reads as sensory overwhelm, not coldness, though Vee took it for rejection.
admitted.detail_quote: In a room like that I listen as hard as I know how and I still can't hear you.

admitted.text: Daphne reads as the older figure entrusted with a child, and the arrangement looks troubling.
admitted.detail_quote: But that was the arrangement: an older student, to help the child find his feet.

admitted.text: Sheri reads as Pace's one unimpressed, plain-spoken friend, the one who asks nothing of him.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't want him, she wasn't impressed by him, and she'd say so to his face

admitted.text: She seems to see Pace's evasion more clearly than he does.
admitted.detail_quote: Then not saying it matters more to you than having her.

admitted.text: Randi reads as someone who survives by showing a flawless face and hiding the real self behind it.
admitted.detail_quote: He could have the face. The face was very good. The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Randi seems constrained by class and sorority respectability, with Brooke making explicit the social price of being seen as queer.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got a position in this house, and you've got her. You need to choose.

admitted.text: Her "it's for the threesome" framing seems to be a cover story for wanting Vee for herself.
admitted.detail_quote: For the threesome. For when she's ready. Somebody has to get her used to my mouth.

admitted.text: Underneath the performance she seems to have fallen in love with Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: She loved Vee and she had told her so, more than once.

admitted.text: Randi reads as a gifted guide who loosens Vee's shame while also steering where it goes.
admitted.detail_quote: Nothing." It came out thick. Then she laughed, wet, and the laugh nearly came off. "I'm fine. It's hormones.

admitted.text: She seems jealous of Vee's place with Pace and is quietly punishing him for it.
admitted.detail_quote: She had come from Vee's table this morning to his, and told him, and watched him be glad.

admitted.text: Randi reads as deeply shaped by her parents' coldness and fraud, performing a safe heterosexual fairytale that leaves her untouched.
admitted.detail_quote: This was the best the acceptable world could do for her.

admitted.text: John reads as polished and accomplished but holding something back, a lover who never reaches Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: This man had taken a beautiful woman to bed, brought her pleasure, but never found her underneath.

admitted.text: Brooke reads as a warm but watchful authority who keeps track of everything in her house.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: Her warmth seems to wrap a real threat to Randi's standing.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got a position in this house, and you've got her. You need to choose.

admitted.text: Cassie reads as loyal and protective; she spends her strength quietly on Vee's behalf.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend

admitted.text: She seems to sense early that Vee is drifting away into Randi's orbit.
admitted.detail_quote: the whole word, flat and finished, the word for a longer parting than a Wednesday.

admitted.text: Meg reads as the steady, unhurried one among Vee's friends.
admitted.detail_quote: Meg was the calm one, dark-haired and level, a girl who ate like she had all night and let a sentence finish before she picked it up.

admitted.text: Kayla reads as an exuberant, nonstop talker who is warm and nosy.
admitted.detail_quote: Kayla let nothing finish. She was round-faced and blonde, a head of curls that moved when she did, and she was always moving

admitted.text: Theo seems a decent boy who took Vee's rejection gracefully.
admitted.detail_quote: And I said let's be friends, and now we're friends, and he waves.

admitted.text: The bench: the hidden apparatus of the game, patiently waiting for its next subject.
admitted.detail_quote: it would sit there in the middle of the room, full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The white-gold bracelet: a binding she never takes off and keeps out of her parents' sight.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi felt her own bracelet, plain white gold, locked on her wrist, and kept it out of the light.

admitted.text: Simpson's paradox: each pair in the triangle reads one way, while the whole tells a different truth.
admitted.detail_quote: Each year on its own, the first man is the better hitter. Put the two years together and the second man is.

admitted.text: The bathroom drawer: Pace's wordless way of making room for Vee in place of a declaration.
admitted.detail_quote: He'd given her the top one. The easy one. The one your hand goes to first.

admitted.text: the green panties: Vee's offered appetite, later becoming the object through which Randi feels excluded and jealous
admitted.detail_quote: the panties Vee had handed him the first night. Deep green satin with dark lace. Its edges dangled from her clenched hand.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: Vee rationing Pace's presence, a scent standing in for the word he won't say.
admitted.detail_quote: It had promised him close and there was no one close.

admitted.text: the burgundy dress: Pace's ability to make Vee's hidden abundance publicly legible and unapologetic
admitted.detail_quote: All of her was there, gathered up and set out like it had nothing to apologize for.

admitted.text: the borrowed black heels: Randi's authorship of Vee's reconciliation and the hidden erotic charge traveling with her advice
admitted.detail_quote: Same feet, baby. Same size, same everything.

admitted.text: the coat with nothing underneath: Vee's attempt to answer a crisis of language by making her body the entire declaration
admitted.detail_quote: She had brought something he could not refuse.

admitted.text: Will Vee ever learn that she was chosen in a game Randi and Pace made together?
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable

admitted.text: What caused the scar on Pace's thigh?
admitted.detail_quote: He kept it there under his, on the thing he wasn't going to tell her about yet

admitted.text: What happened with Daphne that taught Pace both to respect closed doors and to fear saying love?
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: Will Pace ever give Vee the direct declaration he now knows she needs?
admitted.detail_quote: He had believed keeping it unspoken would limit the hurt if she left.

admitted.text: Will Randi choose her place in the house or Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: You've got a position in this house, and you've got her. You need to choose.

admitted.text: Will Randi come back to Pace after weeks of silence?
admitted.detail_quote: He had not seen her since the November morning she came down his hall with Vee's green in her hand.

admitted.text: Will Vee ever tell Randi that she recognized Miranda's name in the PPP records?
admitted.detail_quote: she didn't tell Randi, then or after, what she'd seen.

admitted.text: What will Vee make of Pace's pleasure in her taste, and will she bring it to Randi?
admitted.detail_quote: looking for something it did not name, and found — maybe — under the taste that was only him, a faint edge of sharp and salt

admitted.text: What will happen when Pace and Randi meet at the same table in front of Vee's friends?
admitted.detail_quote: Wednesday night. He's taking us all to dinner. Everybody. You two, Cassie, and Randi, Theo maybe.

admitted.text: What meaning will Vee finally give the kiss she initiated with Randi?
admitted.detail_quote: Vee kissed her best friend until the thing in her chest had somewhere to go.
